routes.description: Establish that scientific explanation and divine agency are compatible, and that a personal creator provides an integrated explanation of rational intelligibility, apparent design, fine-tuning, moral significance, meaning, and the possibility of Christian revelation and miracles.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if theism remains compatible with scientific mechanisms, supplies warranted explanatory advantages over impersonal naturalism, and provides a coherent evidential bridge from a creator to the specifically Christian claims of incarnation, resurrection, redemption, and ultimate justice.

motionBridge.description: Show that science has not displaced God and that Christian theism can still explain the principal phenomena identified by the motion.

centralBridges.description: Explain why rational minds, intelligibility, consciousness, and personhood are grounded more adequately in a personal ultimate reality than in mindless processes.
Connect biological information, cosmic order, and fine-tuning to purposive agency while distinguishing that inference from an appeal to temporary scientific ignorance.
Distinguish regular natural mechanisms from creator agency so that divine action and miracle claims are conceptually compatible with scientific inquiry.
Provide a warranted transition from generic creator theism to Christian revelation, resurrection, forgiveness, moral accountability, and ultimate justice.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Account for objective meaning, enduring hope, and human relational significance without treating their desirability alone as evidence of truth.
Clarify how explanations by mechanism and explanations by agency can coexist without assigning the same explanatory task to each.

routes.description: Establish that natural mechanisms and selection effects explain or undercut the cited evidence for God, that positing a conscious creator compounds rather than resolves the explanatory burden, and that meaning and morality do not require Christian theism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the principal theistic inferences from rationality, design, fine-tuning, miracles, morality, and meaning lack sufficient warrant, while naturalistic accounts remain coherent and the specifically Christian claims require evidence not supplied by their explanatory or emotional appeal.

motionBridge.description: Show that the phenomena in the motion neither require God nor provide adequate grounds for accepting specifically Christian theism.

centralBridges.description: Explain apparent biological design and truth-tracking cognition through natural selection without introducing a designing intelligence.
Show why a conscious creator carries an explanatory burden at least as demanding as the natural phenomena the creator is invoked to explain.
Use observer selection and naturalistic alternatives to challenge inferences from intelligibility and fine-tuning while separating unanswered questions from evidence for God.
Require independent evidence for miracles, incarnation, resurrection, and a morally attentive Christian God beyond generic cosmic order or the desirability of religious hope.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Supply non-theistic bases for personal purpose and moral consideration, including evolved cognition, chosen projects, and concern for suffering.
Maintain the distinction between whether a belief offers comfort, hope, or justice and whether the belief is evidentially warranted.

sections.title: Rationality, Minds, and Cosmic Intelligibility
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether rational persons and a lawlike, intelligible universe require grounding in a prior mind or can be accounted for through evolution and observer-selection conditions.

sections.title: Design, Origins, and Fine-Tuning
sections.rationale: This section contains the principal clash over biological information, apparent design, cosmic beginnings, fine-tuning, creator complexity, anthropic alternatives, and the evidential use of unresolved scientific questions.

sections.title: Scientific Explanation, Divine Agency, and Miracles
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether mechanistic science excludes divine agency and whether alleged special divine acts are coherent exceptions within a regular creation or unsupported violations of scientific expectations.

sections.title: Christian Revelation, Resurrection, and Redemption
sections.rationale: The motion concerns Christian theism rather than an unspecified creator, making the bridge from cosmic intelligence to incarnation, resurrection, forgiveness, judgment, and the character of God independently load-bearing.

sections.title: Meaning, Morality, Hope, and Justice
sections.rationale: This section compares theistic and naturalistic accounts of purpose, moral consideration, human value, hope, and ultimate justice while preserving the distinction between existential desirability and evidential truth.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Evolutionary naturalism threatens confidence in human reasoning because survival-oriented, mindless processes do not necessarily select for truth, thereby undermining the rationality presupposed by science.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Discovering natural mechanisms does not eliminate God because explanation by a creator as agent operates at a different level from scientific explanation of how natural processes work.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: The information-processing language and digital database of life are more intelligible as products of mind than as products of unguided matter and random natural processes.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: A personal creator would be expected to leave evidential traces, and the universe's mathematical describability, fine-tuning, and sophistication constitute such evidence rather than proof.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: In a broken world where much injustice remains uncorrected, the resurrection grounds the rational possibility of ultimate justice that atheism does not provide.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: If the creator is personal, divine initiative in revealing God through Christ in an intelligible human form is a coherent way for human persons to know God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Miracles attributed to the creator are special exercises of divine power rather than ordinary natural processes, so their claimed occurrence is not conceptually excluded by scientific study of regular processes.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Human consciousness, personhood, relationship, meaning, and enduring hope are more intelligible if ultimate reality is a personal God rather than impersonal matter and energy alone.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Christianity diagnoses humanity's broken relationship with God and offers forgiveness and repair through Christ's death and resurrection as a gift rather than as an achievement of human merit.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Natural selection explains the apparent design of biological organisms without either pure accident or a designer, while positing a designing God introduces a further and harder explanatory problem.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Natural selection can produce truth-tracking cognition because organisms that systematically misperceive consequential features of the real world are less likely to survive and reproduce.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Even if a universe-making intelligence were conceivable, that possibility would not establish the specifically Christian God who monitors private conduct, thoughts, wickedness, and sin.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: The historical existence of Jesus does not establish Christian supernatural claims such as virgin birth, walking on water, or transforming water into wine, which require evidence Dawkins says is absent.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Meaning can arise through evolved brains interpreting the consequences of the world, while people can construct personal purposes without requiring a divinely imposed cosmic purpose.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Fine-tuning does not warrant inferring a conscious designer because the designer would require a larger explanation, while observer selection in a multiverse supplies a naturalistic alternative compatible with our existence.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c01.proposition: A secular moral framework can rationally base moral consideration on capacity for suffering rather than species membership alone, making comparisons between humans and other animals philosophically defensible.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c02.proposition: The universe's mathematical intelligibility does not require a divine mind, because creatures capable of evolving, surviving, and asking explanatory questions could exist only in a sufficiently lawful universe.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c03.proposition: Unsolved scientific problems do not warrant invoking God, as Darwin's natural explanation of apparent biological design demonstrates that phenomena once treated as magic can yield to persistent natural inquiry.
